why: Definition item with one listed theorem: A = type of SubmanifoldData.isGoodPositionChart_iff (universe 0), the explicit chart form 'Dt(z)E in good position to C_z inside Dr(z)E'; it is orthogonal to B, so A_to_B is B_holds (no use of A) and B_to_A re-proves A outright from tangentSpace_eq_coe_submodule (no use of B): both directions vacuous, flagged. The substantive result is B_holds: for tame X, a smooth submanifold A and a ∈ A, the project's IsGoodPositionAt agrees with the text's reading in a chart. Differences bridged: (i) B wants V ⊆ dom φ and φ(A ∩ V), the project any data with a ∈ V ∩ dom φ and the shrunk set W = V ∩ dom φ ∩ s⁻¹(V ∩ dom φ) (restrict the sc⁺-retraction to W; W = V when V ⊆ dom φ); (ii) cone T_zO ∩ C_z vs C_z (same on T_zO); (iii) the real one: the project's good complement inside T_zO is only ALGEBRAIC, B's an SC-complement. B ⇒ project is level 0; project ⇒ B uses B's tameness hypothesis: in a tame centred chart N is in good position to C in E (isInGoodPosition_of_tame, i.e. Lemma 4.19 via chart independence), N = Dt(0)E is finite-dimensional and smooth (Lemma 4.7), T₀O = Dr(0)E an sc-subspace, and a closed good complement (exists_proj_goodComplement) cut down to T₀O is an sc-complement (the V3_82 upgrade). So the definitions agree in the text's (tame) setting; for non-tame X the project's notion is a priori weaker.
overlap: B_to_A: 130 shared project theorems, all vocabulary of the statement and of tangentSpace_eq_coe_submodule (retraction/tangent-map/sc-calculus API, SubmanifoldData fields); B_holds additionally reuses non-banned proof lemmas of the project (IsGoodPositionAt.isGoodPositionChart, isInGoodPosition_of_tame → lemma_4_19, exists_chartRetraction, lemma_4_7_ii, exists_proj_goodComplement, IsTame.exists_centredChart).
